title: Dataverse: build solutions with coding agents using the Dataverse plugin and Work IQ
summary: Hold: the briefing understates published consumption charges and incorrectly treats administrator opt-in as a universal requirement for the coding plugin. It also overlooks the allowed-client configuration API and overstates what the Copilot tenant setting blocks.

claims.claim: The Dataverse plugin helps coding agents build Dataverse solutions from natural-language requests.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Dataverse plugin for AI agents helps you develop and manage Dataverse solutions with an AI coding agent. You describe an outcome in natural language, and the agent selects skills and tools to help you achieve it.

claims.claim: The coding-agent capability is admin-opt-in, so nobody can use it until an administrator enables it.
claims.quote: Other tools used by the plugin, such as the Dataverse SDK for Python and Power Platform CLI, authenticate directly and aren't subject to these MCP-specific controls. Their requests still require Dataverse authorization.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to user-opt-in for the locally installed coding plugin. Explain existing environment and privilege prerequisites, and limit tenant consent and environment client allowlisting to Dataverse MCP. Separately describe Work IQ's production defaults and exceptions from https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/business-applications-work-iq/default-settings.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The licensing model for the described plugin, MCP and Work IQ workflows is not yet published.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to mixed. State the applicable Power Apps, Dynamics 365 or Power Platform environment plan from the plugin coding-agents prerequisites, separate coding-agent charges, and Copilot Credit consumption for Dataverse MCP and direct Work IQ API connections. Replace the wholly unanswered licensing question with any specific remaining entitlement uncertainty.

claims.fix: Narrow 'No separate charge is published in the preview documentation' to 'The Dataverse plugin preview pages publish no plugin-specific price as of November 2026; underlying services and coding-agent charges still apply.' Explain the published consumption meters separately.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls: 'None of the switches'
claims.claim: No API is documented for configuring allowed Dataverse MCP clients.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients ... Operations supported: POST GET PATCH DELETE ... isenabled | Edm.Boolean | Display name: Is Enabled
claims.fix: Document the allowed-client REST side: PATCH [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients(<allowedmcpclientid>) with body {"isenabled": false} to disable a client, or true to enable it. Cite this Web API reference and the allowedmcpclient table reference. Remove 'None of the switches has a documented API'; keep any server-wide API gap separate.

claims.claim: Allowed MCP client records are available through Advanced Settings.
claims.quote: Select Advanced Settings. The list of available clients is shown. Open the client record you want.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools. Select Work IQ MCP. Review its current availability. To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: No equivalent API for the Work IQ MCP server's Microsoft 365 Block action is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP server block access API PowerShell admin tools. Opened manage-ai-experience-access; searched results for Agent 365 server management and Work IQ policy. No equivalent Work IQ server Block call found.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; controls[4].api; controls[4].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: There is no separately documented plugin-wide switch deciding who can use the locally installed coding plugin.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse plugin coding agents security governance admin switch licensing service principal. Opened agents-plugin/, coding-agents and security-governance; documented gates are identity privileges and tool-specific MCP controls, not a plugin-wide switch.

claims.claim: Turning off the Microsoft 365 tenant setting overrides every environment's features.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access. ... Work IQ participation settings serve a different purpose and don't prevent agentic access.
claims.fix: Limit the cascade statement to the documented Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat/Dataverse data-sharing connection. Explicitly say it is not a universal block on agentic environment access, the separate Work IQ MCP server, or directly authenticated plugin tools; use the corresponding server, App Access and identity controls.

claims.where: Governance controls: App Access Control path

claims.quote: Sign in to the Power Platform admin center. Select Security > Identity & access. Select App Access Control.

claims.where: Governance controls: App Access Control applicability
claims.claim: App Access can narrow which applications access data in an environment.
claims.quote: App Access is the mechanism used to choose which applications, including agentic applications such as Copilot Cowork, are allowed to access data in a particular environment.

claims.claim: Business-skill access uses Dataverse security roles including Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: An administrator must assign users the Skill Sharing Role, either directly or through a team. Users must also have the security role that the skill is shared with.
claims.fix: Point this sentence to Create and use business skills > Share a business skill, not the Sales agent enablement page, which does not mention Skill Sharing Role. Clarify that role-based sharing requires both Skill Sharing Role and the role receiving the shared skill.

claims.claim: No Dataverse charge is published for the described coding-agent workflow.
claims.quote: The search_data tool uses usage-based Copilot Credit billing rather than a fixed charge per tool call. ... All other tools, including the metadata search tool, follow the text and generative AI tools (basic) Copilot Credit rate per 10 responses.
claims.fix: Replace 'No Dataverse charge is published' with the published Dataverse MCP Copilot Credit treatment. Distinguish the plugin's lack of a separately published price from charges for the tools it orchestrates.

claims.claim: The low, indirect-cost-only rating fits the described MCP and Work IQ workflows.
claims.quote: cost: low; rationale: 'Low. No Dataverse charge is published' versus 'Coding agents or custom integrations that call Work IQ directly: Consumption through that connection appears under Work IQ API.'
claims.fix: Set cost to variable and name Copilot Credits in the rationale. Explain Dataverse MCP billing, direct Work IQ API consumption, separate coding-agent charges and storage implications; the schema reserves low for indirect costs only.

claims.claim: Prepare is the appropriate action rating for this optional coding-agent capability.
claims.quote: action: prepare; Scope: 'Developers and makers with Dataverse environments, using coding agents'; Governance guidance: 'Start in developer environments with interactive sign-in.'
claims.fix: Set action to review for the optional coding plugin: it requires a maker to install and use it. Treat the separate automatic Work IQ environment rollout distinctly rather than implying automatic coding-plugin execution.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist directs readers to audit business-skill use and ownership, but the controls table has no matching monitoring or ownership-review row.
claims.quote: After rollout: 'Audit use of business skills and who owns them.' The table contains participation, tenant audience, Dataverse MCP, Work IQ MCP and plugin-user controls, but no skill ownership or activity-review control.
claims.fix: Add a business-skill access/ownership-review row using the documented Business skills > skill > Share > Manage access workflow. Explain that the Business skills page does not currently show per-skill runtime usage or feedback, and direct usage review to the connected agent's available logs or traces rather than implying a built-in skill-usage report.
